proof.criterion: A1/R2: a Dispatch server with no DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* setting boots, serves the agent-token API, and answers GET /auth/start with a refusal that says browser sign-in is off.
proof.surface: The real envoy-dispatch binary built from this head, as a process on a real Postgres (Debian PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector at 127.0.0.1:5433, the rootless harness docs/solutions/testing/the-real-dispatch-stack-runs-inside-a-legion-pod-with-no-postgres-no-docker-and-no-root-INFRA-42.md describes), driven over HTTP with curl.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && go build -o $TMPDIR/envoy-dispatch ./cmd/dispatch, then env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=$TMPDIR TMPDIR=$TMPDIR DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/dispatch_sandbox_proof?sslmode=disable' DISPATCH_AGENT_TOKEN=sandbox-proof-agent-token DISPATCH_LISTEN_HOST=127.0.0.1 DISPATCH_PORT=18766 DISPATCH_SERVER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18766 $TMPDIR/envoy-dispatch (no DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* at all), then curl -si -H 'Authorization: Bearer sandbox-proof-agent-token' http://127.0.0.1:18766/api/v1/whoami and curl -si http://127.0.0.1:18766/auth/start and curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18766/healthz
proof.observed: The server migrated the database and listened. GET /api/v1/whoami answered HTTP/1.1 200 OK with {"kind":"agent","owner":null,"service":null}. GET /auth/start answered HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable with {"code":"SIGNIN_UNCONFIGURED","error":"Google sign-in is not configured on this server (DISPATCH_SIGNIN_ISSUER, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET, one of DISPATCH_SIGNIN_GROUP or DISPATCH_SIGNIN_DOMAIN)"}. /healthz reported "signin":null.
proof.negativeControl: The same boot with DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID=example-client-id alone and nothing else changed: the process exited 1 with "Google sign-in needs DISPATCH_SIGNIN_ISSUER, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET and one of DISPATCH_SIGNIN_GROUP or DISPATCH_SIGNIN_DOMAIN: DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID set, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_ISSUER, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_GROUP or DISPATCH_SIGNIN_DOMAIN missing", so a half-configured deployment still refuses the boot. GET /api/v1/whoami with a wrong bearer answered HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized {"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","error":"invalid bearer token"}, so the 200 above is the token's and not an open API.

trickyParts: refuseDispatchSeedInSecret calls value.ToStringOutput() on its argument, so a nil args.TailnetAuthKey or args.SignInClientSecret dereferences nil and takes the provider down. Both Secret call sites are gated on their group, not only the environment variables, and TestConstructDispatchSandbox runs the plugin's own Construct path, where such a crash would show.

The sandbox's refusal of a set sign-in input runs before the sign-in group's own checks. Otherwise a sandbox sent signInClientId alone would be refused for signInDomain being unset — the wrong reason — instead of for sending a sign-in input to a deployment that can host no OAuth redirect origin.

A partly set group keeps each input's existing refusal wording and only appends a clause, because TestDispatchResolverRefusesInvalidInputs asserts input-specific substrings (tags + 'at least one', frontDoorToolsImage + 'pinned by digest', signInDomain + 'lowercase DNS name', tailnetDnsName + 'ts.net') and A2 forbids editing them. The clause is added only for an input that is itself unset, so a set-but-malformed value keeps its message exactly.
The four DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* entries render in the place they always held, and no other entry moved, so gcp/testdata/dispatch-pod.golden is byte-identical for a deployment with sign-in on.

TestDispatchSandboxRegistrations removes nine named lines from the registration golden rather than filtering on '-tailnet': ConfigMap example-dispatch-serve carries no such word, and a substring filter would keep it and pass while the sandbox still declared the front door's serve configuration.
deviations: The plan's 'The pod prerequisite for the two Postgres-backed rows' says pgvector is not needed. It is: storetest.Open migrates a template database, and migration 0072_embeddings_core.up.sql runs 'create extension if not exists vector', which fails without it. The harness here installs postgresql-17-pgvector as well, and the two Postgres-backed rows ran with no skip.
